title: Regular Council
summary:
The January 18, 2016 Regular Council meeting closed two public hearings and approved a series of committee recommendations on budgets, development applications and capital expenditures.

- Closed public hearings for Bylaw No. 1571 (3061 Jacklin Rd rezoning to C10, allowing gas stations) and Bylaw No. 1610 (2792 Leigh Rd rezoning to BT1).
- Authorized the Sewage Oversight Committee to pursue an independent sewage treatment analysis and inter-municipal partnership options and consider budget inclusion.
- Approved multiple committee recommendations including accounts payable and five-year financial plans for Land Development, Engineering and Planning.
- Directed staff to prepare bylaws/variances for several rezonings/subdivisions (3483 Happy Valley Rd; 2376 Setchfield Ave; 892 Klahanie Dr; 777 Hockley Ave).
- Approved $40,000 (gas tax) for Langford Transit Exchange shelter foundations.

Approved multiple committee recommendations including accounts payable and five-year financial plans for Land Development, Engineering and Planning. Directed staff to prepare bylaws/variances for several rezonings/subdivisions (3483 Happy Valley Rd; 2376 Setchfield Ave; 892 Klahanie Dr; 777 Hockley Ave). Approved $40,000 (gas tax) for Langford Transit Exchange shelter foundations.

title: Regular Council
summary:
The March 7, 2016 Regular Meeting of Langford Council proceeded with multiple public hearings on OCP and zoning amendments and routine Council business.

- Approved the meeting agenda as amended (added note re: Bylaw No. 1552 proponent representative).
- Held and closed public hearings for a series of OCP/zoning bylaws including 1612/1613 (3483 Happy Valley Rd), 1614/1615 (Hockley Ave sites), 1552 (Peatt Rd/Hockley Ave), 1616 (Klahanie Dr) — several residents spoke in opposition at these hearings.
- Received Committee Resolutions from the Protective Services Committee (building, fire, police five-year plans; open burning schedule; RCMP report).
- Bylaws (speed limit, multiple zoning amendments, road closure) were on the agenda for readings/adoption consideration.

title: Regular Council
summary:
The May 2, 2016 Regular Council meeting approved financial bylaws, awarded a parkway contract, issued a development variance permit, and completed routine legislative business.

- Issued Development Variance Permit DVP16-0005 for 566 Treanor Ave to reduce the rear setback to 1.2 m.
- Awarded West Shore Parkway Segment 1 contract to Windley Contracting Ltd for $1,353,288 (+ GST), funded from the New Building Canada Infrastructure Grant.
- Approved the 2015 Statement of Financial Information (SOFI).
- Approved the Briar Patch Trail name for the trail beside Pritchard Creek at 935 Latoria Road.
- Gave readings/adopted a package of bylaws (Bylaws 1608, 1614, 1615, 1620, 1628–1637) including the 2016–2020 Financial Plan and related fee/tax bylaws.

title: Regular Council
summary:
Council met July 19, 2021 to hold public hearings and consider multiple planning and committee recommendations.

- Approved the agenda as amended (added items and re-ordered bylaws).
- Held public hearings for four zoning bylaws (including Bylaw No. 1919 — City Centre Pedestrian); members of the public raised concerns about building heights and notification timelines.
- Directed staff to prepare a rezoning bylaw for 2165 & 2167 Bellamy Rd and to notify consideration of a Development Variance Permit.
- Directed staff to proceed with a 3-year Temporary Use Permit process for Station Ave commercial/tourism uses and advanced First Reading consideration for Bylaw No. 1994 (648–660 Granderson Rd).
- Received committee and board minutes and approved Council minutes from June 21 and June 24, 2021.

title: Special Council

- Adopted Bylaw No. 1802 (Langford Building Bylaw No.1160, Amendment No. 11, 2018).
- Approved the meeting agenda; meeting was adjourned at 5:34 p.m.

title: Regular Council

- Adopted OCP Amendment Bylaw 1873 (as presented) and approved Procedure Bylaw 1701 (reduced meetings to monthly and suspended committees).

- Awarded detailed design/tender contracts for the Peatt at Brock Road roundabout and Florence Lake Road improvements, to be funded from the Road DCC program.
- Approved the Goldstream Farmers Market Agreement 2020–2022 including tasting and sales of alcohol; directed staff to take no action on Walfred Road streetlights and Setchfield/Lakewood crosswalk requests.

title: Regular Council
summary:
Council met August 15, 2016 and approved multiple bylaws, permits, contracts and event permissions affecting land use, transportation and parks.

- Gave readings/adopted multiple bylaws and zoning amendments including Bylaw 1646 (rezoning 967A Isabell Ave — second & third readings), 1623, 1624, 1644, 1651, 1652, 1654 and 1655.
- Approved contract awards and design work for Dunford and Bellamy bikelane projects and contracted On Point Project Engineers for design ($45,000) funded by Bike BC and Gas Tax.
- Approved lane closures for the Langford Car Show & Shine, waived fees for the Thunder Bowl event, and pre-approved site preparation for the Rugby Canada training facility.

title: Special Council
summary:
Council received a presentation on the Capital Integrated Services and Governance Initiative and provided feedback to the project team.

- Project consultants (Circle Square Solutions / Urban Systems) clarified the initiative examines shared services and potential service models — not amalgamation.
- Council provided feedback on what has been working well in Langford and identified priorities and issues to be addressed regarding integrated services and governance within the CRD.

title: Regular Council
summary:

title: Special Council
summary:
Council held a special meeting on March 26, 2020 and enacted two bylaw actions.

- Adopted Bylaw No. 1701 (Procedure Bylaw amendment) to permit electronic participation for all Council members during a WHO-declared pandemic or a local state of emergency.
- Gave Bylaw No. 1899 (Municipal Park Regulation Amendment) first, second and third readings to permit the Parks Manager to post notices, close parks/trails/beaches and enforce park-use restrictions.
- Approved the agenda as presented.
- Adjourned the meeting at 1:21 p.m.

Gave Bylaw No. 1899 (Municipal Park Regulation Amendment) first, second and third readings to permit the Parks Manager to post notices, close parks/trails/beaches and enforce park-use restrictions. title: Regular Council
summary:
The December 5, 2016 Regular Council meeting approved multiple zoning bylaws, issued two development variance permits, and removed the Dust Control Bylaw from the agenda following developer engagement direction.

- Adopted Zoning Bylaws No. 1552, 1660 and 1661; gave first reading to Bylaw No. 1667.
- Issued DVP16-0017 (Bombardier Court cul-de-sac waiver) and DVP16-0018 (various Goldstream Ave / Trans-Canada Hwy parcels).
- Parks decisions: awarded Bear Mountain maintenance contract ($296,988.52 for 2017), approved Parks capital/operating budgets with a $150,000 backup generator cost increase, and hired a hydrology consultant ($6,300) to register wells.
- Protective Services referred dust management to the West Shore Developers Association and removed the Dust Control Bylaw (No. 1666) from the agenda.

title: Regular Council
summary:
The December 19, 2016 Regular Council meeting adopted finance and transportation recommendations and advanced 2017 engineering budgeting for referral to the finance process.

- Adopted the City of Langford Contaminated Sites Accounting and Reporting Policy (POL-0156-FIN).
- Approved City disbursements for September–November 2016.
- Directed staff to NOT install speed bumps on Braeburn Avenue; approved 3 permit parking stalls on Grainger Road at a cost of $540 funded from the Traffic Sign budget; removed the 40 km/h signs on Amy Road and retained 50 km/h on Sooke Lake Rd.
- Approved entering a tri-party agreement framework for a four‑bay transit exchange at Westhills (subject to BC Transit) and referred the funding request to the 2017 budget process.
- Approved in principle the 2017–2021 Engineering Department capital and operating budgets and referred them to the Director of Finance for budget consideration.

title: Regular Council

title: Special Council
summary:
Council met in a Special Meeting and addressed the CRD Regional Growth Strategy, local ALR exclusions, a CRD water pump station request, and commuter rail exploration.

- Accepted the CRD Regional Growth Strategy (Bylaw No. 4017) and recommended its adoption to the CRD Board.
- Directed staff to work with SD62 and property owners to prepare a new ALR exclusion application for 940 and 960 Latoria Road, request ALC reconsideration, and report back to Council.
- Agreed to make lands at LOT 1 (2131 Bear Mountain Parkway) available for a CRD water pump station and reservoir and to count those lands toward the CD12 zone 40% open space requirement.
- Expressed interest in further exploring commuter rail service on the E&N corridor between Langford and Victoria as an inter-municipal or transit-commission model.

title: Regular Council

title: Regular Council
summary:

- Adopted four bylaws: Streets & Traffic amendments, Animal Responsibility & amendments, Langford Station bylaw and Sewer Utility amendment.
- Directed staff to notify issuance of a 3‑year Temporary Use Permit consideration for a home‑business at 116‑1064 Gala Court; refused the TUP request for 1041 Springboard Place.
- Received the interim Housing Target Progress Report (Sep 1, 2025–Feb 28, 2026) and directed staff to post and lobby the Province to pause Langford's Housing Target Order until provincial housing funds are reinstated.
- Approved reimbursement to the Tri‑Way Neighbourhood Association for legal fees (to be paid from Council contingency) and removed section 1(j) from the Manufactured Home Park Redevelopment Policy.
- Appointed Chief and Deputy Chief Election Officers for the 2026 municipal election.

title: Regular Council
summary:
The May 21, 2019 Regular Council meeting adopted multiple bylaws, approved financial reporting, declared a climate emergency, and declined CRD funding and land participation for a regional foodlands trust.

- Approved the 2018 Statement of Financial Information (SOFI).
- Declared a climate emergency and committed to work toward carbon neutrality.
- Directed staff to tell the CRD that Langford will not fund or provide municipal lands for a CRD-operated foodlands trust.
- Passed a motion limiting any new CRD services/taxes (citing an 11.4% CRD tax increase) until existing initiatives are completed and costs clarified.
- Adopted/advanced multiple bylaws (including Page Avenue road closure and zoning amendments; waived a public hearing for Bylaw No.1851).

title: Committee of the Whole
summary:
Committee received the public budget input and a detailed internal-debt breakdown and directed staff to create governance and remediation plans; it approved a package of 2026 budget reductions and deferrals to lower the proposed tax increase. Key actions: 

- Directed staff to prepare a standing internal-borrowing governance bylaw and a remediation plan for all internal debt balances. 
- Approved reductions and deferrals including a $382,193 reduction to City Hall staffing, removal of the e-bike program, deferral of the Garbage Can Retrofit to 2027, and a Royal Roads grant reduction (≈$65k). 
- Approved transferring $850,000 from Capital Works Reserve to cover 2026 debt servicing and directed an increase of $300,000 in non-property revenues; cut travel/training by $120,000. 
- Deferred the West Shore RCMP business case and set follow-up reporting timetables.

title: Special Council
summary:
The draft Economic Development Strategy was presented by EDCD Consulting and City staff and will be posted for public feedback with a follow-up survey.

- Council received the draft Economic Development Strategy (10 objectives) and noted priority actions including adding economic development staff capacity, creating a commercial/industrial land inventory, and launching a West Shore roundtable.
- Strategy priorities include business retention/expansion, investment readiness (including defence/marine supply chain positioning), downtown revitalization, and community wealth building.

title: Committee of the Whole
summary:
- Committee heard a detailed CRD presentation on regional transportation governance and the CRD workbook to inform municipal feedback.  
- Committee received the report and unanimously directed City staff to obtain a legal, governance, funding and service-level review for Langford, aiming to report to the Sept 11 Committee of the Whole.  
- Staff confirmed CRD's engagement timeline (workbook due Sept 29; CRD analysis to November); City staff will provide additional commentary and options at Sept 11 and Sept 25.  
- Major themes: funding tools, municipal autonomy vs regional authority, data/timing concerns (2014 plan vs new O/D survey), and how BC Transit / DCCs interact with any new regional model.  
- No financial commitment was made at this meeting.

- Tabled DVP23-0007 (2038 Troon Court); Councillors K. Guiry and K. Yacucha opposed the tabling motion.

title: Committee of the Whole
summary:
The Committee received the presentation of the draft 2024–2028 Financial Plan (including the proposed YMCA acquisition) and heard extensive public input on tax impacts and budget priorities.

- Presentation of the draft 2024–2028 Financial Plan included the potential purchase of the YMCA; staff confirmed the five-year plan still includes that acquisition and noted the City is currently paying $1.9M to Westhills Land Corporation (lease).
- Staff clarified consultant and master-plan costs are funded from surplus/grants and not expected to directly increase property taxes.
- The 2024 budget proposes adding 3 RCMP officers (5 were originally requested in prior materials).
- Public participation focused on concerns about tax increases, requests for 2023 actuals and FOI records, and questions about the YMCA purchase and related capital items.
- A motion (mover Harder; seconder Wagner) requesting staff bring back a report to the next Committee meeting was introduced.

summary:

- Proceeded with Bylaw No. 2160 (Transit‑Oriented Area) and directed staff to draft Bylaw No. 2155 to remove off-street residential parking for properties rezoned after Dec 7, 2023; also directed a review of loading/unloading implications.  
- Directed staff to prepare Small Scale Multi‑Unit Housing (SSMUH) bylaw changes to allow secondary suites across many zones, remove minimum lot size/GFA limits for suites, reduce garden‑suite minimum to 400 m2, permit up to six units near transit, and eliminate certain off‑street parking requirements within 400m of transit.  
- Adopted Bylaws No. 1926 (Subdivision & Servicing), 2175 (Council Procedure), and 2176 (Public Notification).  
- Approved an in‑camera resolution under s.90(1)(k) to discuss preliminary municipal service negotiations.  
- Members of the public raised concerns about reduced parking requirements and setback/land impacts.

Proceeded with Bylaw No. 2160 (Transit‑Oriented Area) and directed staff to draft Bylaw No. 2155 to remove off-street residential parking for properties rezoned after Dec 7, 2023; also directed a review of loading/unloading implications. Directed staff to prepare Small Scale Multi‑Unit Housing (SSMUH) bylaw changes to allow secondary suites across many zones, remove minimum lot size/GFA limits for suites, reduce garden‑suite minimum to 400 m2, permit up to six units near transit, and eliminate certain off‑street parking requirements within 400m of transit. Adopted Bylaws No. 1926 (Subdivision & Servicing), 2175 (Council Procedure), and 2176 (Public Notification). Approved an in‑camera resolution under s.90(1)(k) to discuss preliminary municipal service negotiations. Members of the public raised concerns about reduced parking requirements and setback/land impacts.

title: Regular Council
summary:
Council approved multiple land‑use bylaws and development readings, changed its multi‑family stratification policy, awarded a major road construction contract, and committed regional funding for parks planning.

- Adopted Officers Bylaw No. 2114 and OCP/Zoning amendments (Bylaw Nos. 2149 & 2150) for 2207 Millstream Road.
- Gave Bylaw No. 2165 (775 Latoria Road) first, second and third readings after a delegation and public input.
- Changed policy so multi‑family housing will no longer be required to be strata‑titled; accepted alternatives including a housing agreement and $7,500/unit amenity contribution (amendment to remove the rental requirement was defeated).
- Awarded the Amy Road — West Shore Parkway roundabout contract ($1,059,599 + GST) and increased the project budget to $1,298,500.
- Approved $75,825 funding for the West Shore Regional Parks & Recreation Facilities Master Plan.

title: Advisory Committee
summary:
The Community Advisory Committee recommended Council approve amendments to the Grant in Aid policy (POL-0147-FIN) to broaden eligibility and update application rules.

- Recommended Council approve POL-0147-FIN Amendment No. 1 to expand Grant in Aid eligibility to include School District 62 Parent Advisory Councils and other school-sanctioned committees.
- Added a requirement that eligible entities be Council-approved and have a presence in Langford (Amendment 1); the amendment passed with opposition from M. Morley, K. Yacucha and R. Plomp.
- Directed staff to define "retroactive fees" and to allow certain applications submitted before the deadline even if the event/project took place prior to Council consideration, so long as the activity did not occur before the application deadline (Amendment 2).
- Staff proposed a $10,000 per-application cap and noted a current annual Grant in Aid budget of $80,000.

title: Special Council
summary:
The Special Council meeting approved the purchase of the Westhills Langford Aquatic Centre and several associated financial and administrative actions.

- Declared 840 Arncote Avenue a nuisance and unsafe; imposed a Remedial Action Order requiring cleanup within 30 days or the City will remediate at the owner's expense.
- Endorsed the Economic Development Plan RFP scope of work.
- Adopted Bylaw No. 2187 (Station Avenue Fees and Charges amendment) and adopted the consent agenda minutes.

- Received the report for information; staff presented the dollar scale of options (1% = $622,061 city-wide; ≈$26.41 per average household).
- Staff highlighted reserve pressure (Capital Works & General Amenity reserves declining) and major capital pressures including ERP replacement and childcare/capital projects supported by grants.
- Reduction buckets (11/9/6/3%) were shown with estimated required cuts ($2.57M; $3.81M; $5.68M; $7.5M) and examples of potential impacts (staffing deferrals, parks/tree maintenance, storm/drainage, arena repairs).
- Committee emphasized waiting for public input (budget survey open to March 4; public COTW March 17 for deliberation) before final decisions.

title: Committee of the Whole
summary:
Committee of the Whole received public input on the Proposed 2026–2030 Financial Plan and discussed reduction options for the 2026 tax increase.

- Members of the public urged Council not to cut maintenance or safety-related budgets and to avoid deferring necessary repairs.
- Staff confirmed the proposed 2026 tax increase (reported previously as ~15.13%) and identified funding sources including property taxes, prior-year surplus ($1.73M), grant funding ($1.55M), amenity/DCC and other reserves.
- Staff will report budget-survey results to Committee on March 17 and continue public participation at upcoming meetings in April.
- Staff clarified many capital projects are funded by DCCs, amenity/casino funds, grants or reserves (not immediate property-tax dollars); non-property revenues (e.g., building permits, licence-to-occupy) were discussed as limited options to reduce tax reliance.

title: Special Council
summary:
The council approved the Transportation Master Plan and Active Transportation Plan, accepted the Waste Management NRFP scope, introduced inclusionary zoning and amenity cost charge bylaws, and approved multiple land-use and variance items. Key outcomes:
- Adopted the Transportation Master Plan/Active Transportation Plan and directed phased implementation and advocacy for regional overpasses.
- Received and validated the Waste Management NRFP scope; staff will issue a negotiated RFP with Colwood and target contract award in late summer with a 2027 phased rollout.
- Gave first–third readings to Amenity Cost Charge and Inclusionary Zoning bylaws and established reserve funds to replace the old density-bonus approach.
- Issued a Development Variance Permit for 1436 Pinehurst Place (fence height) and directed notice for variance consideration for the Atkins/Winster properties (RMCP expansion); Council extended the meeting to complete business.
